observations.observation: Super Saiyan Goku Super Saiyan Goku, the guy on the literal cover of the game.
He is the shoto of DBFC like Ryu, Terry, Soul, Bad Guy, or Kazuya in their respective games.
The character they put on the box, the one to teach you the game, balanced, reliable, and dangerous in the right hands.
Let's start with his buttons.
His normals are safe on block and have great range, meaning he can poke you from distances where you think you're safe.
His overhead is plus frames, so even when he goes for the mix and you block it, he's not getting punished.
And the M&H versions of that overhead don't just threaten you, they start combos.
So, you have to respect it every single time.
He also has an overhead cross-up, which means he can hit you from the wrong side and your brain will short circuit trying to block it.
On top of all that, his projectile game is amazing.
Great range, great coverage, and his assists are genuinely good, meaning he fits on almost any team you want to build.
And if you want to just dump resources and end someone's life, his level five solo super is right there.
Consistent combo extensions into massive damage.
He's the starter character that never really stops being good, clean, and reliable.
Super Saiyan Vegeta, Goku's eternal Super Saiyan Vegeta rival and the guy who will never be the main character.
But in DBFZ, Vegeta is a legitimate menace.
His whole game plan is about making you uncomfortable from every range.
He zones you out with projectiles and while you're trying to figure out how to get in, he's ready to punish your super dash on reaction.
You thought approaching was the answer.
Vegeta disagrees, but he's not just a zoner.
Mix in an assist and suddenly Vegeta is running mixups on you.
And because he can get a full combo out of basically anything that hits, every mix is a real threat.
His auto combo into forward is a sneaky tool too.
It leaves him plus on block, meaning he gets to keep his turn even when you defend correctly.
He also has a DP, an actual reversal.
So, if you try to pressure Vegeta, he has an answer for that, too.
And then there's his A assist.
It can be moved and is genuinely annoying to deal with.
Great for extending your own team's pressure or just making your opponent's life miserable.
Oh, and his sparkless loops work anywhere on the screen.
No corner needed, just consistent, repeatable damage wherever the hit confirms.
Finally, Vegeta can be used specifically to switch into a knockdown that benefits another character's game plan.
Great team utility on top of everything else.
Vegeta might not be the main character, but it is your opponent's problem.
Piccolo, the green alien guy who has Piccolo been Gohan's babysitter.
Actually, a really solid character.
Piccolo has a great variety of special moves that cover all kinds of mixups, cross-ups, overheads, command grabs.
He keeps his opponent constantly guessing which one is coming, and that mental pressure adds up fast.
His combo extensions are very solid.
Jump H gives him easy reumps, which means his air combos doesn't just stop.
And thanks to hell zone grenades, he can dump supers for massive damage when the situation calls for a comeback.
Now the really fun stuff.
Piccolo can restand opponents, meaning he can pop them back up mid combo and go straight into a mixup.
You thought the combo was over.
By the way, a assist is genuinely great for controlling neutral.
Stick Piccolo on your team, even if you're not playing him point, and he's already doing work just by existing.
The skill ceiling on this character is somewhat high, and the sauce of the combos is unique.
If you want to invest time into learning optimal combos and setups, Piccolo will reward every hour you put in.
Green and deeply underestimated.
Your opponent will figure it out eventually.
Team Gohan, the kid who was Teen Gohan supposed to take over as the main character after the Cell Saga.
In this game, he is an absolute problem.
Let's talk about his iconic autocombo first.
It steals turns and in the right situation, it can straight up steal games.
If you've played this game, you've been hit by it.
The core of his game plan though is Masendan.
Every optimal team Gohan combo runs through it.
It works everywhere on screen.
And the damage it produces is genuinely insane.
Learning Masiman is the difference between a casual Gohan player and a scary one.
He also has a DP, so if you try to pressure him, he has a reversal option ready.
His level one super is one of the most damaging in the entire game for the meter cost.
And if you have the meter and want to close things out in style, he has access to a level five as well.
Now, Gohan does have a decent projectile and tools to get in, but he has no solo mix.
The good news is that with the right assists behind him, he can mix opponents up extremely effectively.
He just needs the team support to do it.
Team Gohan, peak Dragon Ball Z, peak DBFC.
Frieza, space lizard, galactic tyrant, Frieza fashion icon, a full-on zoner who will make you feel like you're being slowly suffocated from across the screen.
His projectile game covers everything.
Ground key blasts, air key blasts, lingering discs that combo if they hit, quick explosions to check your movement, beam moves for longer range.
Whatever angle you're coming from, Frieza has something pointed at you.
Frieza does rely on assists to get in and start his mix-ups.
His cross-up is slow, so he needs help closing the distance, but base form Frieza is just the opening act because then he transforms into golden Frieza.
The transformation works as both a reversal and a combo extender.
It buffs his damage, buffs his speed, and gives him an extra air dash.

Suddenly, the zoner who needed help getting in can now go from full screen projectile pressure straight into close quarters blockstrings and beating you up close linking button combinations that wouldn't work in base form.
The transformation does have a 50-second timer, though.
Here's a tip most people don't know.
If you tag out while golden, the timer resets.
Switch to another character, come back, and you've got a fresh 50 seconds.
Use that wisely, and Golden Frieza stays on the field way longer than your opponent expects.
Captain Ginu, the most theatrical Captain Ginyu villain in Dragon Ball history.
In DBFC, he is the most complex character in the entire game. honest truth out of the way first by himself.
He calls the Ginu force and that's where everything changes.
Gulo, Rkum, Berter, and Jace come in one after the other in order throughout the match.
Each member has three different moves you can choose from and each of those moves can be delayed.
That's six different options per member changing as the match progresses.
Your combo routes, your neutral tools, your mixup options, all of them shift depending on who's next in line.
The job of a Ginu player is to always know who's coming next and make the right call.
Use them to control neutral, extend a combo, or open up the opponent for a mix.
Now, let's talk about his H button.
It's a load that can be moved and charged.
If your opponent expects it and crouches, Ginu can jump and cross up instead.
He can cancel the charge into a dragon rush into a Ginu Force call and can even use it in the air for more mix options.
His B assist is quietly busted.
A screen covering battery assist.
His level three super lets him rearrange the Ginyu force order.
If you swap bodies with your opponent, their Ginyu can't call the Ginu Force.
You've handed them a useless character while you keep yours.
Trunks Future Trunks, timetraveling swordsman who showed up and killed Frieza in 5 seconds.
His overhead is quick and threatening and the M version is plus on block.
His 3M is crazy, a full screen low.
Your opponent won't be ready the first time.
His key blast is another story.
Lightning fast with massive priority.
In a projectile exchange, Trunks is simply winning and you are simply losing.
His flips are special moves that take real time to master, but if you do, you unlock a completely different dimension of the character.
His level three is a quick grab reversal that genuinely jump scares people in the heat of a match.
But where Trunks truly becomes dangerous, where he's genuinely busted, is as an anchor character.
Trunks burns through meter constantly with his EX moves.
But as a solo character, he makes excellent use of passive key gain, always refilling what he spends.
And if you save sparking for him at the end, your opponent should be worried.
His mixups gain new layers.
His pressure becomes harder to read, and guessing wrong means a full combo.
And he can kill you straight out of a disjointed hitbox at long range.
Pair that with an extremely damaging solo level five and you have a character that wins games by himself when the stakes are highest.
Came from the future specifically to ruin your day.

Combined with team assists, it becomes a genuine mixup tool that's very hard to see coming.
His post level three mix is one of the better ones in the game.
Easy to execute and immediately threaten.
Cell great assists and at his absolute best.

You try to pressure her.

Her jump M hits as an overhead from both sides, and she has a six frame low to go alongside it.

Some of the most damaging corner sequences in the game.

Two characters for the price of one and she's charging you for both.
Gotenks Gotenks, a child with the power of a god and the attention span of someone who had too much sugar.
Let's start with what Gotenks does best, keeping you in a combo forever.

He can cancel certain special moves directly into other special moves, which means his combo loops are long, his meter generation is excellent, and the damage adds up in ways that feel deeply unfair by the end of a sequence.

For the 50/50, Got Tanks uses an assist combined with his auto combo fast and it leads into full damage on hit.
And then there's level one ghosts, a high seating skill that takes real time to learn, but in the corner it jails opponents into a mix they can't easily escape.
One of those tools that separates casual Gotenks players from genuinely scary ones.
He will hold you in a combo until one of you gets bored.
Krillin, the strongest human on earth and most reliable punching bag in DBFZ. an absolute Krillin killing machine.

Senzu beans heal blue recoverable life for him and his teammates.

Kid Buu, the purest, most distilled form of evil in Dragon Ball Z.
Fast, Kid Buu unpredictable, and constantly in your face.
His M button is his foundation.
Both on the ground and in the air, it's quick, long-range, and safe on block.
Kid Boo doesn't have a traditional mixup, but he has ways to crack you open.

Now, the honest part, his anti-airs are genuinely bad.
His two H has a small hitbox that whiffs more than it should, and his anti-air grab is slow and unreliable as a punish tool.
His corner game is where he really shines, though.
Good routes, solid damage, and enough tricks to keep opponents guessing.
Kidbu, a somewhat honest character with just enough gimmick to keep things interesting.
Majin Buu Majin Buu, a bubblegum pink ancient demon who likes candy and turning people into food.

Your opponent thinks the combo is ending.
Now they're standing up and guessing again.
The problem is getting his turn.
Without a Cyberman on screen, his neutral is genuinely poor, and his stubby normals doesn't help either.
You must know how Cyberman routes work to avoid dropping combos.
By the way, his corner loops are very easy and damaging.
